cells.tense: You are standing at the start of something, and the start is still open.
cells.act: let yourself want it, plainly, to yourself
cells.ask: Notice what you'd genuinely like tomorrow to hold, and don't argue yourself out of it. Name it once, quietly, to yourself. No plan, no telling anyone, nothing to act on yet.
cells.core:
You can stand at the start of something and not force it into a shape. So much is still possible, and you're letting it stay that way — present with it, no verdict rushed. That isn't stalling. It's the moment before a choice turns all that possibility into one real thing, and it's how a person comes to know which thing they actually want.

Among what's open to you, there's a possibility you'd feel worst about losing. You know which one. Want it plainly, to yourself, this week — no plan attached. Say it once, quietly, and keep it. No telling anyone, no acting. What's left will sit undecided longer than comfortable, and you'll feel you ought to have picked already. You don't. Wanting first is how one comes to know which was theirs.

cells.tense: You will keep the seed open until the next possibility arrives, and the next.
cells.act: put your own name on what is already yours
cells.ask: Take one thing already within reach and do it the way only you would. No explaining. You don't have to prove it's the right choice — just do the version that is yours.
cells.core:
Where you stand at the start of things, the start is being kept open on purpose. Everything could still become anything, and you guard that — the next version a little wider than this one, nothing hardening into a thing that would need tending. It feels like keeping your options alive. Seen from outside, it can look like nothing is ever permitted to land.

There's a second half to being a seed: letting what you already are come through in one actual act, even while the rest stays open. Pick something already within reach this week and do it the way only you would, without proving it's the right choice. Not a decision about your whole direction — one thing, done as yours. What you are gets to show instead of staying potential, and the ground beneath all that openness turns out solid.

cells.tense: You stopped arriving at the start, and you are still standing at that other door.
cells.act: look at the same thing longer, until it shows you more
cells.ask: Choose something near you that might be a beginning — a thought, an idea, a small plan — and stay with it longer than usual, beyond where you'd turn away. See what it can be. Decide nothing yet.
cells.core:
Where things could be starting, nothing gets near the start line. What you consider arrives pre-shut — you look at the options you can already handle, and the question of what could grow from a thing doesn't get asked. The caution is steady. The room in it has closed.

Look longer. Choose something near you that might be a beginning — a thought, an idea, a small plan — and stay with it beyond where you would normally turn away, until it shows you something it hadn't shown you before. See what it can be this time. Not a decision, just a longer look. Possibility comes back through the eyes before it comes back through the hands, and one longer look is enough to start.

cells.tense: You are opening doors without seeing them, and your hand is already on the pen.
cells.act: picture it a year on, turned out well, and keep the picture
cells.ask: Hold one thing in your life as it might look a year ahead, turned out well. Keep that picture without turning it into a plan and without telling anyone. See if it holds.
cells.core:
You're opening doors for yourself — a different idea, a slower pace, a word at the right moment — and if asked, you'd say you were just going along. The choices are being made, and some are good ones. What's missing is your name on them. You file them under circumstance. The choices don't.

Go back to wanting, no plan attached. Hold one thing in your life as it might look a year ahead, turned out the way you'd like, and keep that image. Don't make it a plan and don't tell anyone; keep it light, a month if it holds itself. Your hand is already in what's becoming; this just lets you see it there. The next time a door opens, you'll know who opened it.

attempts.check: The draft's weakest claim is that the person is genuinely open and ready rather than simply uncommitted; a reader could rightly say they are just indecisive or avoiding a choice.
